findings.where: outputs/robgrade/NI_POLICY.md:P1 and section 3; outputs/robgrade/ni_policy_review/RESPONSES.md:codex3 and subsequent escalations
findings.claim: The blanket prohibition on contextual PY/PN remains contrary to the guidance. Disclosing or escalating this departure does not make it guidance-compliant. It can inflate both proposed judgements and the NI-driven stratum.
findings.guidance_basis: Handbook 8.2.3 permits NI only when a reasonable PY/PN judgement cannot be made from the circumstances. Its experienced-trials-unit example explicitly permits PY for concealment without reported concealment methods. [Cochrane Handbook](https://training.cochrane.org/handbook/current/chapter-08)
findings.failing_test: Documented large regulatory trial conducted by an experienced trials unit, concealment methods unreported, and a reviewer supplies a justified contextual 1.2=PY; other D1 answers are 1.1=Y and 1.3=N -> permit PY, giving LOW and ni_driven=false. The policy instead requires NI, giving SOME_CONCERNS and ni_driven=true.

findings.claim: Applicability is computed before correcting asked NA answers. Correcting 2.4 from NA to NI opens 2.5, but 2.5 remains incorrectly normalized to NA. The assessment then stores SOME_CONCERNS while ni_label's second normalization computes HIGH. The round-3 fix therefore does not consistently enforce its own normalization rule.
findings.guidance_basis: Full guidance Table 6, final Part 1 row: 2.3=Y/PY, 2.4=Y/PY/NI and 2.5=N/PN/NI gives High. With 2.6=Y, Part 2 does not reduce it. [Full guidance, p.32](https://facenteconsulting.com/wp-content/uploads/20190822_RoB_2.0_guidance_parallel_trial.pdf#page=32)
findings.failing_test: assessment with D2 answers {2.1:Y, 2.2:Y, 2.3:Y, 2.4:NA, 2.5:NI, 2.6:Y, 2.7:NA} -> normalized 2.4=NI and 2.5=NI, stored judgement HIGH, favourable judgement SOME_CONCERNS. Current stored judgement is SOME_CONCERNS. Also assert normalization is idempotent; asked 3.2=NA currently becomes NI on the first pass and N only on the second.

findings.claim: An invalid stored judgement can remove a previously eligible pair without triggering the frozen-eligibility or recomputation guards. Only the INSUFFICIENT status is compared; pairs_for excludes other invalid judgements before rebuild validates them.
findings.guidance_basis: NI_POLICY section 4 promises refusal when a stored judgement differs from recomputation or eligibility changes. RoB 2's three judgement categories do not authorize treating a malformed value as an exclusion. [Handbook 8.2.3](https://training.cochrane.org/handbook/current/chapter-08)
findings.failing_test: Freeze a matched TEST D1 record with answers {1.1:Y,1.2:NI,1.3:N}, judgement SOME_CONCERNS and ni_driven=true. Change only its judgement to 'LOW_typo' -> scoring must refuse. Currently check_answers_frozen passes and pairs_for moves the record into excluded, bypassing recomputation.

findings.claim: The frozen-cohort check can be bypassed by omitting entire topics through the optional SLUG arguments. A selected subset still overwrites the standard output and is presented as the pre-registered TEST analysis.
findings.guidance_basis: NI_POLICY section 4 specifies all four comparators and promises refusal of cohort changes. Neither RoB 2 nor the stated policy supplies a rule permitting post-registration topic selection for that analysis.
findings.failing_test: With all four registered topics available, main([PREREG_SHA, TOPICS[0]]) -> refuse incomplete confirmatory coverage, or explicitly produce a separate exploratory subset report. Currently it scores only that topic under the standard pre-registered report heading.

findings.claim: The registration anchor is caller-controlled. Any later clean commit, including HEAD after changes to policy, answers and comparator inputs, passes when supplied as PREREG_SHA. This verifies consistency with a nominated snapshot, not immutability relative to the original registration.
findings.guidance_basis: NI_POLICY's Status paragraph identifies the commit adding the policy as the registration and promises refusal of subsequent changes. The implemented ancestor check does not establish that identity.
findings.failing_test: Register at commit A; subsequently change protected inputs or policy and commit B. check_prereg(B) -> refuse because B is not the registered anchor A. Currently it accepts B, and frozen_object also reads the replacement answers from B.

findings.claim: The accepted AND-to-OR change enforces a mathematically incorrect contract: one constant rater does not make Cohen's kappa undefined. It can make kappa uninformative, but the coefficient remains defined when expected agreement is below one.
findings.guidance_basis: Cohen's coefficient is (observed agreement − expected agreement)/(1 − expected agreement). RoB 2 provides no alternative definition that makes either constant marginal automatically undefined. [Reference implementation](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/_modules/statsmodels/stats/inter_rater.html)
findings.failing_test: kappa([('LOW','LOW'),('LOW','HIGH')]) -> kappa=0, with observed and expected agreement both 0.5. Current result is kappa=null. A test expecting undefined solely because either rater is constant has the wrong expected value.

findings.claim: The reported confidence intervals use the variance under the null hypothesis kappa=0, rather than the general sampling variance of the estimated kappa. Consequently the advertised asymptotic 95% intervals are wrong away from the null.
findings.guidance_basis: The supplied expression uses products of marginal probabilities and omits the estimated-kappa factors. These are the null-variance terms, distinguished from the variance used for confidence intervals in the [reference implementation](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/_modules/statsmodels/stats/inter_rater.html).
findings.failing_test: Pairs comprising 45 LOW/LOW, 5 LOW/HIGH, 5 HIGH/LOW and 45 HIGH/HIGH -> unweighted kappa=0.8, general asymptotic SE=0.06 and rounded CI=[0.682,0.918]. Current code gives CI=[0.604,0.996].
